runs.text: Why does a real program usually mix the three ways of thinking?
A real kiosk has calculations, best written as pure functions; things with state, such as the inventory, best written as objects; and an edge that reads and shows, which is imperative and short.
Because each part of the program expects a different kind of change.

justification.text: Calculations grow with new operations, things with state grow with new kinds, and the edge is short.

runs.text: Because that way it is faster.

justification.text: Speed does not decide the way of thinking.

runs.text: Because none of them is any good on its own.

justification.text: Each one works on its own; mixing them makes use of what each one makes easy.
